item.title: Americans don’t have to choose between our AI future and ripping off copyright owners
item.description: The DOJ's embrace of fair use for AI training breaks with the White House's own framework, as OpenAI, Microsoft and news groups battle over copyright.
item.content:encoded:
One of the biggest court battles over artificial intelligence (AI) is putting an age-old legal principle to the test — and raising important questions about the Trump administration's AI policy.

Several news organizations, including The New York Times, are suing OpenAI and Microsoft for using millions of newspaper articles to train AI systems. The newspapers argue that the tech firms violated basic copyright protections. The tech firms contend that training their models on those articles qualifies as "fair use," a longstanding principle that allows copyrighted material to be used in certain ways without permission from or compensation to the copyright owner.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has sided squarely with OpenAI's position — breaking with the administration's previously more balanced stance on the issue. The DOJ filed a statement of interest embracing an extreme vision of fair use that would grant AI companies virtually unfettered access to copyrighted material for commercial training, without obtaining permission from or compensating the creators whose works fuel these systems.

MIKE DAVIS: THE TRUMP DOJ SHOULD WITHDRAW ITS STATEMENT OF INTEREST IN THE OPENAI LAWSUIT

This expansive interpretation threatens to turn a narrow copyright exception into a blanket exemption for the world's most powerful and profitable industries.

The DOJ's reasoning is that requiring a copyright license for material used in AI training would impose high costs on AI developers. It claims those costs could make it harder for small companies to compete and hamper U.S. AI leadership and national security.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

Those concerns deserve consideration. But the DOJ's aggressive arguments in the brief depart from more measured guidance elsewhere in the administration. The White House's official AI framework acknowledges valid arguments on both sides of the copyright debate.

Likewise, the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, adopted by G20 ministers at the Commerce Department's recent Innovation Ministerial, recognize that the intersection of AI and copyright poses "complex legal and policy questions." The principles note the "essential role" of copyright protections in supporting creators and call for respecting IP as a pillar of G20 AI policy.

MUSIC INDUSTRY FENDS OFF FLOOD OF AI MUSIC 'STEALING' THE CHARTS

The DOJ statement also overlooks how its stance could favor larger AI companies over smaller firms and startups. Several AI startups have argued that paying for the material they use provides more reliable access to training material, reduces legal uncertainty and improves models. Other companies have emerged to aggregate copyrights and make licensing easier.

It's particularly problematic for large AI companies to complain about paying for access to copyrighted materials. They are among the best positioned to pay for those materials, and doing so would help develop the kind of licensing markets they claim are lacking.

OBAMA CRITICIZES TRUMP ON APPROACH TO AI, ESCALATES WARNING FOR STRONGER REGULATION

And even if national security were a legitimate justification, the government could not simply disregard property rights. The Constitution and other laws require just compensation when private property is taken for public use, and intellectual property rights are still property rights. Letting AI firms appropriate creators' IP without permission or compensation would be akin to letting data center builders seize private land without paying fair value.

If courts adopt the DOJ's position that fair use protects AI developers in virtually all circumstances, it would reduce incentives to create new works. Copyrights encourage creative work by assuring writers, artists and other creators that their work can't be easily stolen or copied. Licensing those rights allows creators to earn a living and underpins over $1 trillion in U.S. economic activity.

Weaker copyrights could result in fewer human-created books, articles, research papers, films and songs. Ironically, that could eventually leave AI systems with fewer and lower-quality materials to train on – a scenario that serves no one's interests.

All of this is why the Trump administration would be wise to follow its own AI framework and let the court system evaluate AI copyright disputes case by case, rather than arguing for unfettered fair use exceptions.

Policymakers also have a role to play. One promising bill is the bipartisan CLEAR Act. Introduced in February by California Democrat Sen. Adam Schiff and Utah Republican Sen. John Curtis, the CLEAR Act would require AI developers to publicly disclose the copyrighted works used in each new generative-AI model's training dataset.

The proposal would not settle whether any particular training practice qualifies as fair use. But it would give creators more information about whether their work helped train an AI system, enabling them to pursue appropriate compensation or other remedies when they believe their rights have been violated.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That kind of targeted reform offers a useful model for copyright enforcement in the age of AI. Rather than treating licensing as an obstacle to innovation, policymakers should foster a market where AI developers can efficiently license copyrighted material while respecting creators' rights.

AI innovation is vital to America's future. But America's creative industries still depend on strong copyright protections. Policymakers need to promote both.

item.title: Ranking the top six 'Grand Theft Auto VI' in-game radio stations, from V-Rock to Vice City FM
item.description: "Grand Theft Auto VI" packs 22 radio stations, and this ranking crowns V-Rock No. 1, with Emotion 98.3 yacht rock and Vice City FM's 80s vibes close behind.
item.content:encoded:
If you’ve played even five minutes of "Grand Theft Auto VI" since its release, you know just how immersive this video game is.

There are miles of swamps and beaches to explore, realistic NPC interactions and I even made an entire article about how realistic the game’s version of South Florida is when compared to its real-life counterpart.

But one mechanic that has been included in the new game that’s been around since the early days of the series are the radio stations, and "GTA VI" has the most diverse radio dial yet.

REDDIT'S BIRDING COMMUNITY GOES WILD AS UNIQUE 'GRAND THEFT AUTO 6' FEATURE COMES TO LIGHT

All in all, there are 22 unique radio stations in the game, and each of them offers a different soundtrack to your wheeling and stealing as you traverse through Leonida.

Being a huge fan of the series and music in general, I thought it would be fun to rank my six favorite "GTA VI" radio stations.

This wasn’t easy, as there are a ton of great stations to choose from, and I even had to omit a few that I really liked (sorry, Back Country Radio).

With that said, let’s rank the best that "GTA VI" has to offer in the form of music.

By virtue of hitting the "quantity over quality" metrics, Flash FM sneaks its way onto the list at number six.

Don't get me wrong, there are heaps of awful songs on this station, but there are some gems in there too.

Echosmith, Foster The People, Gwen Stefani, and MGMT will have Millennials bobbing their heads as they commit vehicular homicide (in the game), and newcomers like Ella Langley and Addison Rae offer enough to be passable cruising songs when there's nothing else on.

Flash FM isn't the stalwart it was back in the '80s for "Grand Theft Auto: Vice City," but there is enough fun to be had here for this station to find its way into the rotation.

This one might be a bit of a nostalgia pick for me, but I don't care.

Having grown up and gone to high school in South Florida, a lot of the songs on this station were popular right around the time my life was centered around algebra tests and getting rejected by chicks, so playing a game where I can drive around a virtual representation of my hometown while blaring rap songs that were popular 15 years ago is an auto win.

If you're into 2000s and 2010s rap, you'll probably have your radio dial locked on Dirty South Classics, with heavy hitters like Lil Wayne, Outkast, Drake, Rick Ross and even Jay Z being well represented here.

There is no better feeling than cruising Miami Beach at night listening to "No Lie" by 2Chainz, and it's even cooler when that is also a core memory from your adolescence, minus the cocaine and dead hookers.

Now we are getting into rarified air, and Vice City FM begins a string of stations with way more good than bad on them.

For those of you who wanted the '80s vibes of "Vice City" to carry over to the new game, you're in luck.

MIAMI HEAT UNVEIL VICE CITY COURT FOR 'GRAND THEFT AUTO VI'-THEMED CLASH WITH MILWAUKEE BUCKS

Vice City FM is a carryover from the old Playstation 2 game, and the songs you'll find on here will have you thinking you hopped in a DeLorean and landed in 1986.

Genesis, Culture Club, Lionel Richie, Billy Idol, The Cars and so much more, you'll be pulling out the AquaNet and legwarmers before your first hour of gameplay.

The neon lights of South Florida mesh perfectly with the 80s vibes, and this station makes for a cool nighttime drive soundtrack.

For an added bonus, Weird Al Yankovic is one of the in-game DJs, which I thought was a nice touch.

Metal, metal and more metal. That's what you're going to find on The Chamber.

While I'm partial to the older stuff, this station has a great mix of classic and newer metal to bridge the generational gap for headbangers.

If you're a spiritual Boomer like me, you'll be happy to know acts like Iron Maiden, Judas Priest, Megadeth and, of course, Metallica are littered all over The Chamber.

New-school metal disciples will be pleased to hear the likes of Linkin Park, System of a Down, Tool and Sepultura mixed in.

Committing virtual crimes is so much more fun when it's set to the brutal riffing and blistering solos of Judas Priest's "Freewheel Burning," but don't just take my word for it, try it yourself.

And hey, the station is hosted by Slayer's Tom Araya and Kerry King, so you know it's curated by two legends.

Can you name a better combination than the sun-soaked streets of South Florida and some soothing yacht rock?

Of course you can't, which is why Emotion 98.3 is sitting in the silver medal spot for "GTA VI" radio stations.

Emotion makes its triumphant return as one of the stations featured in "GTA: Vice City," and its setlist will have you looking for the nearest super yacht to steal so that you can enjoy the songs properly.

You want soft rock? How does Ace, Chicago, The Doobie Brothers, and Bruce Hornsby sound?

And that's just the tip of the iceberg.

I spent my entire life being serenaded by these guys while navigating the intracoastal waterways of South Florida, and now I get to do it in a video game.

Life sure is sweet sometimes!

It was never going to be anything else.

If you played "GTA: Vice City," you know how legendary this station was.

Well, it's back and better than ever, featuring a wide range of classic rock artists that offer the best company on any long drive around Leonida.

There are too many bangers to even count, but I'll try: Def Leppard, AC/DC, Aerosmith, Dire Straits, Foreigner, Blue Oyster Cult, Motley Crue, Styx, and ZZ Top, just to name a few.

Seriously, I haven't even mentioned another half dozen artists who rank as some of my favorites of all time.

Oh, and they have Van Halen, too. In case I needed to nerd out any more than I already am.

I also love how they included several Tom Petty songs, given his connection to the Sunshine State.

Finally, the station is hosted by Lindsey Buckingham of Fleetwood Mac fame and Michael Freaking McDonald.

When the king of Blue Eyed Soul is spinning tunes, it's probably a station worth listening to.

item.title: Las Vegas Grand Prix betting guide: How to bet Saturday night's race on the strip
item.description: Las Vegas Grand Prix betting picks: Kimi Antonelli to win at +470, Lando Norris podium, Charles Leclerc podium at +350 and Oscar Piastri as biggest mover.
item.content:encoded:
Vegas doesn't do anything quietly, and the Las Vegas Grand Prix is no exception. The lights are on, the casinos are packed and Formula One cars will be screaming down the Strip at more than 200 miles per hour Saturday night. It's the one race on the calendar that feels like a show as much as a sporting event.

The betting board fits the setting. You can lay heavy juice on the favorite, or you can do what Vegas is built for and take a few swings. The race also has one more ingredient that makes it great to bet: chaos. Las Vegas averages 48.7 overtakes per race, more than Monza, Baku or Jeddah. The starting grid is a suggestion here, not a guarantee.

Here's how to bet the Las Vegas Grand Prix, from the race winner to a couple of fun swings further down the board.

WHAT IS A PARLAY BET? — HOW PARLAYS WORK, PAYOUTS AND RULES EXPLAINED

Antonelli was the fastest driver in qualifying, 0.258 seconds clear of Verstappen. A five-place penalty for an extra engine component dropped him to sixth. Oscar Piastri, Carlos Sainz and Lance Stroll took 10-place penalties, and Piastri starts 17th after qualifying seventh.

Odds via FanDuel

This is the bet. The fastest car on the track is starting sixth, and you're getting almost 5-1 on it.

Antonelli has already won this year's drivers' championship, and he's chasing his 10th win of the season. He out-qualified everyone by a quarter of a second, and Mercedes brought a turbocharger upgrade this weekend that only he is running. Russell is on the older spec.

Starting from behind hasn't slowed him down this year. He won at Monza from 19th on the grid and finished fifth in Baku from 16th. Both are high-speed, low-downforce tracks, just like Vegas. Throw in a circuit that produces almost 50 overtakes per race, and five spots isn't much to make up.

Norris is the steady play. He starts third, he has four straight top-five finishes, and he took pole here last year before finishing second, a result later wiped out by a post-race disqualification.

He's also been quick all weekend. Norris set the fastest second sector in qualifying and finished just 0.093 seconds behind Verstappen's lap. In Brazil, he beat Verstappen to the line by 14.6 seconds. Starting on the second row of a track where passing is easy, a top-three finish is a reasonable ask.

NFL BETTING STRATEGY GUIDE: HOW TO BET ON FOOTBALL

This is the Vegas swing.

Ferrari had a rough qualifying session, with both cars knocked out in Q2. After the penalties, Leclerc starts 10th. That's exactly why the price is +350, and exactly why I'm interested.

Leclerc has finished in the top four in all three of his Las Vegas starts. He's led 13 laps here, the third-most of anyone since the race began. He has six podiums this season, finished second at the U.S. Grand Prix and has finished in the top five in seven of his last eight races in North America.

Some drivers just have a feel for a track. Leclerc has one for this one. At 7-2, it's worth a bet.

Here's a fun one. Piastri qualified seventh, then a 10-place engine penalty dropped him to 17th on the grid.

The pace is there. He was within about a second of pole in qualifying, and he's running the same McLaren that Norris has on the second row. A fast car starting 17th on the highest-overtaking track of the season is a natural fit for this market. If he finishes anywhere in the top 10, he'll likely be among the biggest movers on the night.

Verstappen has won here twice, in 2023 and 2025, and he starts on pole. I understand why he's the favorite.

But -130 means risking $130 to win $100 on a single race, at a track where the polesitter has less protection than almost anywhere else, with the fastest car in the field coming up behind him. Under the Vegas lights, I'd rather bet on chaos than lay juice on the chalk.

item.title: Trump says Roger Clemens should be in the Baseball Hall of Fame 'immediately,' won't fully back Barry Bonds
item.description: Fresh off pardoning Pete Rose, President Donald Trump said Roger Clemens belongs in the Baseball Hall of Fame immediately, citing his seven Cy Youngs.
item.content:encoded:
After giving a "complete and total pardon" to Pete Rose, President Donald Trump now has his eyes on getting another baseball legend into Cooperstown.

Trump said that seven-time Cy Young Award winner Roger Clemens should be in the Baseball Hall of Fame "immediately." Trump noted that Clemens has never been proven to have taken performance-enhancing drugs.

"Roger Clemens has never been proven to have taken drugs, and he swears that he didn't. And he went through committees and everything else, and they — he actually won a court case. And Roger Clemens said and stated strongly he never took drugs," Trump said during an appearance on Fox News' "Saturday in America."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Trump was referencing the court case in June 2012, in which Clemens was acquitted of all six counts of perjury, making false statements and obstructing Congress after a retrial over his denials of using steroids. Trump gushed over Clemens' illustrious resume.

Nicknamed "Rocket" for his overpowering fastball, Clemens won seven Cy Youngs, the most in the history of the sport. He won the 1986 AL MVP, was an 11-time All-Star and a two-time World Series champion, and won the ERA title seven times.

While Trump was steadfast in his belief that Clemens belongs in the Baseball Hall of Fame, he did not offer the same endorsement for Barry Bonds.

"Barry Bonds, I think (denied taking drugs) too. But a lot of, I mean, look, he was such a great player, you know, he was a great player before the so-called drug excursion, if that ever took place," Trump said.

TRUMP SAYS HE'LL GIVE ROGER CLEMENS THE PRESIDENTIAL MEDAL OF FREEDOM: 'THIS SUPERSEDES ANYTHING I'VE DONE'

Bonds has never admitted to knowingly taking performance-enhancing drugs. The San Francisco Giants legend testified before a federal grand jury in 2003 that he unknowingly used a substance called "the clear," which is a designer anabolic steroid.

"The problem is he just looked like he took drugs," Trump said with a laugh.

"With Barry, it’s a little bit different (than Clemens) because there was very strong testimony and everything else," Trump said. "But I would consider. His numbers are so big, he was a great player and then he became a beyond great player."

Bonds' 762 home runs, 2,558 walks, 688 intentional walks and 162.8 bWAR are all MLB records. He was a seven-time MVP and a 14-time All-Star.

Bonds received 66% of the vote in his final year on the ballot, short of the 75% required to earn induction.

Clemens peaked at 65.2% in his final year on the ballot. Unfortunately for him, he isn't eligible to be voted in again until 2031 because he received fewer than five votes from the 16-member Contemporary Baseball Era Committee in Dec. 2025. As a result, he became ineligible for the next three-year cycle under Hall of Fame rules. Bonds, who also received fewer than five votes from the committee, isn't eligible until 2031, either.

item.title: Sammy Kershaw responds to 'sellout' critics after attending 2026 CMA Awards red carpet
item.description: Sammy Kershaw says talks with the Country Music Association went in a positive direction after he claimed he and wife Mendy were denied red carpet access.
item.content:encoded:
Sammy Kershaw is addressing critics directly who suspect that he "sold out" for attending the 2026 Country Music Association awards.

Speaking to Fox News Digital on the red carpet, the legendary country music singer explained how he spoke with the association after taking to social media to air out his grievances about the association allegedly denying him and his wife access to walk the red carpet.

"Well, it went great, and I'm not going to tell you all the details of what was said. All I can tell you is that I know things were going in a positive direction. So, when we decided that I was going to come to the show and walk the carpet, there's a few people out there that said things like, 'Oh, he sold out' and this and that. But that's not how I look at it," Kershaw began. 

ELLA LANGLEY DOMINATES CMA AWARDS WITH MAJOR WINS AS TAYLOR SWIFT MAKES STUNNING RETURN TO STAGE

"The way I look at it was, there was me and the CMA. And we came together and talked. We're moving in the right direction to a greater time in country music," Kershaw continued.

Without giving away details of the conversation, the country music star emphasized that both parties stayed for the whole conversation. "Nobody got up and walked away," he said.

Kershaw said that he didn't intend to hurt anyone with his Instagram post, but he was "heartbroken" by the association's decision.

"And then all of a sudden a lot of other people's fans came aboard. The fans, country music fans are country music fans, and they will bat for anybody in country music," Kershaw said. "Sometimes they'll get rough, but they came together for this because it was more than a carpet walk."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

On Nov. 5, Kershaw uploaded a lengthy statement to Instagram, stating that the Country Music Association was not allowing him or his wife, Mendy, to walk the red carpet.

Kershaw claimed that he adjusted his tour schedule to accommodate this year's award show after being "strung along" for several months, assuming that they were invited.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"After more than 50 years in this business, many millions of records and singles streamed and sold, more than two dozen Billboard charted hits, a CMA Horizon Award nomination, being a lifetime CMA member, that they presented to me in 1992, and being asked to donate my time to play CMA Fest, I would hope I’ve earned the opportunity to walk the red carpet alongside my wife, as we’ve done before," Kershaw wrote.

He added, "I love country music, but never in a million years would I think that a successful country music entertainer (and I’m not the only one) would not be able to walk the red carpet. It’s extremely hurtful, embarrassing and very disappointing. I guess the next time I attend the CMA’s, it will be in tribute after I’m gone, if I’m lucky."

Country music stars poured into his comment section, supporting his message.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Riley Duckman wrote, "If you haven’t earned the right to be there then nobody has… disappointing to say the least."

Granger Smith added: "So sad for country music. I grieve for the old CMA. … many of us wouldn’t be here without artists like you…"

item.title: Retired FBI agent warns NCIC breach could threaten police safety during traffic stops
item.description: Retired FBI agent Jason Pack warns a hack of the National Crime Information Center could endanger officers at traffic stops if records were altered.
item.content:encoded:
A retired FBI supervisory special agent warned Saturday that a cyber intrusion into the bureau's National Crime Information Center (NCIC) could endanger police officers during traffic stops if hackers altered records inside the database.

Jason Pack, a former FBI supervisory special agent who worked in cybercrime and public information, told Fox News Digital that the bureau's incident response team must quickly determine whether data was manipulated inside the system, which feeds criminal records to patrol cars nationwide.

"What they worry about is if any of this data has changed, then it might affect officers' safety on the side of the road," Pack said, noting there is no indication yet that any records were altered or that the system is experiencing an outage.

FBI PROBES SECOND CYBERATTACK IN MONTHS AS HACKERS BREACH KEY CRIME DATABASE, SOURCES SAY

Three sources familiar with the matter told Fox News that hackers breached the NCIC, marking the second cyberattack against the bureau in months. The FBI is investigating how the intruders gained entry and whether any information was compromised.

In an interview with Fox News' Kayleigh McEnany on Saturday morning, President Donald Trump said he had "just heard" about the intrusion, adding, "I will say that it’s not good. I don’t like that."

Pack described the NCIC as "America's computer for law enforcement," explaining that roughly 56 state terminals feed data out to hundreds of thousands of patrol car computers, so officers can check warrants, criminal histories, missing children, gang members and suspected terrorists.

FBI SAYS SOURCE OF ITS JOBS PORTAL BREACH STILL UNKNOWN AS HACKERS ALLEGE EMPLOYEE DATA COMPROMISED

While the database does not hold classified intelligence or sensitive FBI investigative case files, Pack said it stores personally identifiable information, including names, dates of birth and Social Security numbers.

Investigators will examine IP logs and metadata to determine whether attackers exploited a compromised password among the system's more than 100,000 users, breached a state terminal or infiltrated through a third-party vendor, Pack said, adding that cyberattacks have accelerated to "machine speed" as criminals increasingly use artificial intelligence to probe for vulnerabilities.

"You have this cat and mouse game where cybersecurity experts are trying to patch the vulnerabilities that they find. They're looking for their own vulnerabilities at the same time, they have to play defense against the criminals who are out there trying to steal information or do harm to our systems. I think we're just seeing now this speed of these intrusions ramp up a lot," Pack said.

TECH OUTAGE CASCADE EXPOSES US VULNERABILITIES TO FOREIGN CYBER THREATS

The intrusion follows a September cyberattack in which the extortion group ShinyHunters breached an FBI job portal website and claimed to steal personal records belonging to bureau employees.

The latest incident also comes as a Government Accountability Office (GAO) report found 17 of 22 government agencies were not in compliance with federal cybersecurity regulations.

The FBI did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the NCIC breach.

Fox News Digital's James Cirrone and Greg Norman-Diamond, and Fox News' David Spunt contributed to this report.

item.title: Utah vs TCU prediction, odds and best bets: Utah faces a big time trap spot
item.description: Utah vs. TCU betting preview: Why TCU +7.5, the Horned Frogs moneyline and the under 46.5 are the plays for Saturday night in Fort Worth.
item.content:encoded:
Utah has done everything right this season. The Utes are 10-0, No. 2 in the College Football Playoff rankings and riding a 16-game winning streak dating to last season. They're in line for a first-round bye, and in Morgan Scalley's first year, they're the best story in the Big 12.

That's also why Saturday night in Fort Worth is a dangerous spot for the Utes.

Over the last two weeks, Utah has played two games that would drain any team. It beat rival BYU 28-20 in the Holy War, then had to rally for a 40-39 win at Arizona which was a bit of a letdown spot in its own right. Now the Utes are on the road again, for a 9:00 p.m. ET kickoff against a TCU team fighting for bowl eligibility, with one of the best defenses in the country, in what will surely be a rowdy atmosphere.

FIVE COLLEGE FOOTBALL BETS FOR SATURDAY, INCLUDING TWO ROAD DOGS THAT ARE BEING SLEPT ON

The market sees an unbeaten team against a .500 team. I see a letdown spot, a defense built to slow Utah down and a lot of bad luck about to turn around.

Utah -265 | TCU +215
Spread: Utah -7.5 (-105) | TCU +7.5 (-115)
Total: 46.5 (Over -110 / Under -110)

Saturday, Nov. 21, 9 p.m. ET, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth, FOX

This is about as lopsided as a betting market gets. Between 82% and 90% of the spread tickets are on Utah, and the Utes have drawn between 73% and 84% of the money.

The line has moved around with that action. Utah opened at -6.5, climbed as high as -7.5 and has settled between -7 and -7.5 depending on the book. The public is backing the undefeated team with the shiny ranking, and the books are happy to take it.

I love a classic contrarian spot, and in this one, I'm happy to go the other way.

WHAT IS A TEASER BET? HOW TEASERS WORK IN FOOTBALL AND BASKETBALL BETTING

Spots like this are where unbeaten teams lose.

Utah has been in close games almost every week since late September, and the last two were especially challenging. Winning a rivalry game against BYU and then rallying on the road at Arizona takes a lot out of a roster. This is the third straight week the Utes have played a meaningful, high-stress game, and it's another road trip with a late kickoff.

Don't get me wrong, I fully understand that Utah's offense is still dangerous. Devon Dampier has accounted for 31 touchdowns, 22 passing and nine rushing, and the Utes are scoring 37.9 points per game, 15th in the country. But this is the kind of game where good teams can look flat for a half, and against this defense, a flat half can be enough to put the Utes in trouble.

ESPN DISMISSES UTAH UTES AS NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP CONTENDERS DESPITE BIG WIN OVER BYU: 'THEY WON'T WIN'

Utah's offense isn't the only elite unit in this one. TCU's record hides how good its defense has been. The Horned Frogs allow just 15.2 points per game, 12th in the country, and they rank ninth nationally in net adjusted EPA per play allowed.

That's the matchup that matters. TCU has been at its best against offenses like Utah's. Under Sonny Dykes, the Horned Frogs are 17-7 straight up and 15-8-1 against the spread against teams averaging at least 425 yards per game. Dykes is also 6-3 against the spread as an underdog of 3.5 to 10 points, right in the range of this line.

This is the stat that makes the case, and I promise it's not a stretch. TCU has lost five games this season, and all five were decided by one score. Against Power 4 opponents, the Horned Frogs are 1-5 in one-score games, the most such losses of any Power 4 team. They've battled, but things have consistently gone against the Horned Frogs in close ones.

On the other side, Utah is 4-0 in those games. One could make the argument that good teams find a way to win those games, and that's true. But it's also true that there is some inherent luck in close games, and expecting that to always go your way i playing with fire.

Close-game records rarely hold over a full season. TCU hasn't been five losses worse than its opponents. It's been a handful of plays worse. Utah hasn't been four wins better, either. Eventually those coin flips start landing the other way, and a home game against a conference opponent with national championship aspirations is a good place for that to start for TCU.

WHAT IS A MONEYLINE BET? — HOW MONEYLINE ODDS, PAYOUTS AND FAVORITES WORK

It's only fair to make Utah's case too. The Utes are 8-2 against the spread and 7-1 as favorites of 6.5 or more. They score at an elite rate, and their defense allows only 18.6 points per game, 21st in the country.

TCU's offense is the real concern. The Horned Frogs score just 23.4 points per game, 103rd nationally, and they've been inconsistent all season. If Jaden Craig, who has thrown one interception over the last three games, can't move the ball, TCU's defense will eventually wear down.

That's why the points matter. I don't need TCU to outscore Utah. I need its defense to keep this within a score. If you're not a true believer in TCU at home, take the points.

This is the main play. Utah is in a letdown spot, the public is lopsided and TCU's defense is good enough to keep this close. The Horned Frogs have lost five games by a combined handful of plays. Getting more than a touchdown at home with that profile is the best number on the board.

If you believe in the letdown, take a smaller piece of the upset. At +215, the moneyline implies TCU wins about 32% of the time. With a top-12 scoring defense at home against a tired team on the road, that feels low.

The total fits the same story. TCU games have gone over just twice in 10 tries, and the Horned Frogs have averaged only 18.3 points per game in conference play. The early under action has been heavy, with every tracked ticket and dollar on the total backing the under.

item.title: No 10 BYU survives Kansas in triple overtime thriller to keep College Football Playoff hopes alive

item.content:encoded:
It is better to win ugly than to lose pretty, and BYU's season-saving triple-overtime win was not pretty.

No. 10 BYU (9-2) staved off Kansas (4-7) in a 31-29 thriller on Saturday afternoon at David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium to keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive. For a moment, it looked like the Cougars were going to come away with the win without requiring overtime.

Kansas tied the game at 16-16 with a touchdown with just over four minutes left in the game, but BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier led the Cougars into field goal range, leaving kicker Matthias Dunn a 37-yard field goal attempt with time expiring.

However, instead of walking Kansas off in regulation, Dunn yanked the field goal attempt wide left as time expired, forcing overtime.

The Jayhawks got the ball first and quarterback Isaiah Marshall took the game over with his legs. On third-and-10, Marshall scrambled for 12 yards to keep the drive alive. BYU forced another third down, but Marshall again escaped the pocket and scored a touchdown, putting Kansas up 23-16 after the extra point.

It took BYU just three plays to respond, as a 23-yard pass from Bachmeier to wide receiver Kyler Kasper set up a 2-yard touchdown run from Bachmeier. After Dunn's extra point, the game was tied at 23-23.

BYU got the ball first in the second overtime and scored in just four plays. Running back LJ Martin converted from 11 yards out, but in the second overtime, both teams must go for two if they score. BYU's defense was on the brink of closing the game out, as it forced a fourth-and-5 on Kansas' opening series. However, Marshall threw up a prayer to the end zone as he was being pressured, and wide receiver Nahzae Cox went up and hauled it in for a 20-yard touchdown to tie the game 29-29.

Ty Pennington has built and maintained a successful career with his extreme home makeovers, but there's one renovation trend he believes homeowners are taking a little too far these days.

In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, Pennington — who has recently partnered with Insmed on the "Suspect BE" campaign to encourage people with unresolved respiratory symptoms to pursue further testing — weighed in on where homeowners should and shouldn't put their renovation budgets, calling out oversized kitchen islands packed with redundant appliances as a trend that has crossed into overkill.

"I would probably say the island with three dishwashers," the veteran HGTV star, 62, said when asked about renovation trends that go overboard. "It's maybe a little excessive. This is coming from somebody who was a personal dishwasher for many years of my life."

JOANNA GAINES REVEALS WHY SHE AND CHIP WALKED AWAY FROM 'FIXER UPPER' AT THE HEIGHT OF ITS SUCCESS

"There is a point that you almost get too big," he continued. "Is there an island that's almost the size of a small court? Possible. So I think sometimes we may be sort of outgrowing things. We may be just going too big. I know that's hard to believe, but I think sometimes we've got to scale back not only in budget, but also maybe in size. Cozy is cool."

While Pennington advocates for dialing back the scale, he still acknowledges that kitchens and bathrooms remain the smartest investments for homeowners looking to build equity.

"The most expensive are the kitchens and the bathrooms, but I do think they're kind of necessary if you plan on selling, because that's what people look at first," he explained.

When tackling home projects and renovation with his wife, Kellee Merrell, Pennington said compromise can prevent them from budding heads.

"Sometimes you have to divide and conquer," Pennington said. "If somebody is passionate about a certain project that they know exactly what they think they want it to look like, sometimes you have to just use a different room in a different project. We don't always agree on everything. I don't think that happens in any aspect of life. What I try and do is lend my perspective and also throw out a couple of crazy ideas that hopefully sometimes lead to something sort of midway between."

"When you're dealing with a spouse and their plans, you sort of have to just be like, well, you just have to trust," he added. "And I think that's the key."

These days, Pennington is splitting his time between his home in Georgia with Merrell and his mother’s home in Florida, where he has stepped into a caretaker role.

Nearly 20 years ago, his mother was officially diagnosed with bronchiectasis, or BE—a chronic, progressive lung condition that causes permanent widening and scarring of the airways.

Pennington, who has partnered with biopharmaceutical company Insmed as a spokesperson to raise awareness and educate others about BE, said his mother's diagnosis—combined with his own past health scare involving a life-threatening throat abscess—fundamentally shifted his perspective on life.

I have a little bit of regret because we didn't realize what was going on for so long with my mom. We only have so much time in life. Let's make the best of it."

Watching his mother navigate a chronic respiratory condition has also shifted his own mindset when it comes to staying physically active.

"I think it's really important to make sure you take time to focus on your body and make sure you're constantly moving," he said. "The one thing I've noticed with my mom is because you're battling and struggling with some health issues, you don't keep your body as strong as it should be because you get winded."

item.title: Jerry Jones says Cowboys had 'no record' of fight incident that resulted in fan's death at home loss vs 49ers
item.description: Jerry Jones says the Dallas Cowboys had no record of an incident before a fan died after their 49ers game at AT&T Stadium, pledging to investigate.
item.content:encoded:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said Friday that the team had no record of an alleged fight that resulted in a fan’s death during the team’s game against the San Francisco 49ers, adding that he believed the fan was hospitalized because he "didn’t feel good" at the game—a claim that has raised questions about what happened at AT&T Stadium.

Police say Mario Narro fell during a fight at the stadium. According to reports, he remained at the game but later complained to friends of pain. Paramedics at AT&T Stadium treated Narro before he was transported to a hospital, where he died Wednesday, his family says.

Jones addressed the death during his Nov. 20 appearance on 105.3 The Fan’s "K&C Masterpiece," saying he had only just received information about the situation.

COWBOYS OWNER JERRY JONES UPDATES TIMELINE FOR NFL'S 18-GAME SCHEDULE, FLOATS PRESEASON REDUCTION

"No record of an incident at the game, and I just got that information... so we had no record of an incident, and we'll be obviously looking into that," Jones said, when asked about the Arlington Police Department's report of a fight that allegedly occurred around kick-off time.

Jones added, "My understanding is that the individual went to the game, and didn't feel good at the game, and then left and then had been hospitalized. But we weren't aware of any incident involving a fan at the game."

Jones then pointed to the stadium’s surveillance capabilities, describing them as substantially improved from a decade or more ago. He also cited the roughly 6,000 workers on game days and said an incident escaping the team’s notice would be unusual.

"We have quite a surveillance at every aspect of our game, so it is really a rare if we didn't know of any incident... We have 6,000 workers on game day," Jones said, adding his team would "of course" send any of that footage to the police department.

Asked whether the Cowboys would provide footage to police if needed, Jones replied, "Of course."

Meanwhile, the fan’s family is asking for help bringing their loved one home.

COWBOYS GREAT MICHAEL IRVIN OUTLINES FRANCHISE'S TIMELINE TO RETAIN 'AMERICA’S TEAM' STATUS

In a GoFundMe campaign titled "Bringing Mario Home to Rest," organizer Lois DeLara identified herself as Mario’s niece and said he traveled to Texas for a football game before his unexpected death.

The fundraiser seeks assistance with funeral and memorial costs, transporting his remains home and expenses incurred by family members making arrangements in Texas.

DeLara described the family’s struggle to grieve while facing unexpected financial obligations. The campaign does not provide a detailed account of the incident or a medical explanation for his death.

"You will forever be loved and missed," she wrote.

item.title: NBA Hall of Famer and Baltimore native Carmelo Anthony joins the mob in scolding Ravens' Marlon Humphrey
item.description: Carmelo Anthony's Instagram rebuke of Marlon Humphrey over his Baltimore crime joke reads as virtue signaling, given the city's grim FBI crime statistics.
item.content:encoded:
NBA legend and Baltimore native Carmelo Anthony loves his city. That much is obvious. But, his lengthy Instagram post scolding Ravens' cornerback Marlon Humphrey following the former first-round pick's joke that Baltimore is "best at making criminals" comes across more as virtue signaling than anything.

Anthony grew up in West Baltimore, witnessed the city's struggles firsthand, and understandably takes pride in the place that helped shape him into a basketball superstar, so being defensive of his city shouldn't be surprising. But there's a difference between defending your hometown and pretending its problems don't exist, aren't that bad, or shouldn't be the subject of any jokes, no matter the level of truth to it.

WHAT IS BALTIMORE BEST AT MAKING? 'CRIMINALS,' SAYS MARLON HUMPHREY WHO THEN FEELS THE HEAT AND CHANGES TUNE

After his comments went viral, Humphrey apologized, was eventually sent home and deactivated by the team for this Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.

"I’ve been here my whole career," Humphrey told reporters. "I’ve spent lots of offseasons here, welcomed a son here. I’m an investor in the city, investor in various parts of the state."

Apparently, those comments, his past work, and apology weren't enough for Anthony.

"I’ve been sitting with this one for a couple of days, because Baltimore isn’t a talking point to me. It’s my blood," Anthony wrote on his Instagram post. "I saw what this city can take from you. I lost friends to the streets, and I watched people I loved get swallowed by a system that was built to swallow them. I know the reputation. I’ve heard every joke and every headline my whole life."

But Anthony's own words also reveal the problem with his criticism.

BALTIMORE DC ANTHONY WEAVER ADDRESSES MARLON HUMPHREY 1-GAME BANISHMENT OVER CITY CRIME REMARKS

He acknowledges losing friends to the streets, watching loved ones suffer, and witnessing the consequences of Baltimore's troubled environment. Yet he's upset that Humphrey dared to characterize the city as a place where criminality is a serious problem?

This was a genuinely heartfelt statement from Anthony, who has clearly experienced the uglier side of Baltimore long before becoming a multimillionaire NBA superstar, but it also proves Humphrey's point that criminality has been an issue for the city.

Also, we have to remember this whole post is in response to a side comment, light-hearted joke, rooted in the truth. That's all. Humphrey didn't call all Blacks criminals. He never said that nothing is being done to fix clear problems with crime. He never devalued the hurt and pain Anthony and others have gone through.

According to Security.org's analysis of FBI crime data for 2025, Baltimore ranked fifth in violent crime per capita and sixth in overall reported crime per capita among America's 50 largest cities.

Its violent crime rate was approximately 1,347 offenses per 100,000 residents.

That's not a flattering statistic, but ignoring it doesn't make Baltimore's residents any safer.

And while Baltimore has made measurable progress reducing homicides in recent years, improvement doesn't erase the fact that residents continue to face disproportionately high levels of violent crime. Going along with the liberal narrative that Baltimore is now safe and shouldn't be subject to scrutiny because there's been a decrease in crime, is just a stupid way to deflect and gaslight those who highlight that crime is still clearly an issue in the city.

So why is Humphrey being treated as though he's committed some unforgivable offense for speaking negatively about the very problems Anthony acknowledges experiencing?

Make it make sense.

Anthony continued saying, "Marlon, I see the apology. I’ll take it, man to man. But Baltimore has been apologized to its whole life. Apologies don’t build anything. Presence does… You don’t get to rep Baltimore on Sundays and talk about it like an outsider on Wednesday."

This is just pure virtue signaling.

Anthony is certainly entitled to defend Baltimore's reputation and advocate for its residents, but demanding that Humphrey demonstrate his commitment to the community, after Humphrey specifically cited his investments and personal ties to the city, seems to be more about policing the cornerback's words than addressing the substance of what he said.

Anthony's post, and others like it, makes it seem like Humphrey is being treated as a traitor to his race for making a truthful joke.

Interestingly, Anthony's argument in his Instagram post becomes even more questionable when you examine the people he celebrates as examples of Baltimore's success.

FBI REPORTS LARGEST DROP IN VIOLENT CRIME AND MURDER SINCE 1937 AS HOMICIDES FALL MORE THAN 18%

Anthony also invoked Baltimore-born boxing star Gervonta "Tank" Davis as an example of the talent and success that can emerge from the city.

There's no disputing Davis' accomplishments inside the boxing ring, but outside of the ring, he's committed to the very criminality Humphrey was joking about.

Davis has faced multiple criminal charges and legal controversies throughout his professional career, including domestic violence allegations and a hit-and-run case.

In 2023, Davis was sentenced to probation, home detention and community service after pleading guilty to charges connected to a 2020 hit-and-run crash in Baltimore that injured four people. He subsequently served jail time after violating the terms of his sentence.

That doesn't erase Davis' boxing accomplishments, nor does it mean he cannot serve as an inspiration to young athletes through his athletic ability and hard work, but glamorizing a boxer with a documented criminal history, while chastising Humphrey for discussing Baltimore's crime problem is an awkward choice, to say the least.

Davis' story demonstrates both the extraordinary athletic talent and criminal behavior that Baltimore can produce, which again proves Humphrey's point.

Again, Anthony's point falls flat.

And while we're discussing uncomfortable truths, Anthony isn't exactly unfamiliar with controversy involving criminal conduct.

In 2004, Anthony was cited on a marijuana possession charge after marijuana was discovered in a backpack associated with him. The charge was later dropped.

That same year, Anthony appeared in the infamous Baltimore-based Stop Snitchin' video, which became associated with an anti-cooperation message toward law enforcement. That controversy was especially troubling because discouraging witnesses from cooperating with police can make it more difficult to prosecute violent offenders and protect communities suffering from crime.

Anthony subsequently distanced himself from the video and its message.

In April 2015, the then-New York Knicks star marched alongside hundreds of protesters through the streets of Baltimore following the death of Freddie Gray, who suffered a fatal spinal injury while in police custody. A year later, he reflected on his complicated relationship with Baltimore police, admitting he used to run from officers and deliberately provoke them as a kid. While acknowledging he had positive relationships with some officers, Anthony declared, "There are good police, and there are f—ed up police. That's the way it is."

To be clear, appearing in that video is not the same as personally threatening witnesses, and a dismissed criminal charge is not proof of guilt, but the episode is relevant when Anthony positions himself as an authority on how Baltimore's crime problem should be discussed.

A city cannot seriously confront violent crime while treating criticism of its reputation as a greater offense than the conditions that created that reputation.

Humphrey's comments are being treated more harshly than the actions of criminals who have wreaked havoc across the city over the years.

Humphrey's comments didn't sit well with his Ravens teammates, either.

"I think he was trying to say it in a joking manner. But it’s not a joking matter. That’s not cool. I think he knows that," veteran defensive tackle Calais Campbell said Thursday.

Head coach Jesse Minter deactivated Humphrey for Baltimore's upcoming game against the Carolina Panthers, sending him home for the week.

"When you say something like that, it’s, you know, it’s not a reflection of our team and our organization and how we want to operate," Minter told reporters Thursday.

Anthony, meanwhile, concluded his statement with a declaration that "Baltimore doesn’t make criminals."

Of course, cities don't literally manufacture criminals. Individuals make choices, and millions of law-abiding Americans live in communities struggling with crime, but pretending Baltimore's longstanding struggles with violent crime are merely an unfair stereotype does a disservice to the people living with those consequences.

Anthony's love for his hometown seems sincere. His emotional attachment to the city is understandable, and his desire to see Baltimore portrayed as more than its worst headlines is understandable, but his public lecture of Humphrey risks becoming precisely the kind of performative virtue signaling that substitutes celebrity outrage for meaningful discussion.

Baltimore deserves investment, opportunity, accountability, effective and supported policing, safer neighborhoods, and politicians who actually want to see the problem resolved.

What Baltimore doesn't need is another famous athlete demanding apologies because someone said something unflattering about a city in which crime statistics remain deeply troubling.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI mania could endanger marriages as relationship coach exposes red flag
item.description: Couples jump into Grand Theft Auto VI's release as relationship expert Matthew Hussey of Los Angeles shares advice on balancing gaming passion with real relationships.
item.content:encoded:
The long-awaited arrival of Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI has become a craze among gamers, and a point of contention between couples.

Ahead of the video game’s release on Nov. 19, couples on social media anticipated how the game might create space in their relationships — with users posting about men gearing up for hours of gameplay and women worrying about the resulting distance.

While some posted videos of men gifting their partners flowers and treats ahead of the download, others took a firmer stance on prioritizing gameplay over relationship time.

'GRAND THEFT AUTO VI' MANIA COMES WITH SERIOUS HEALTH RISKS, DOCTORS WARN

One husband jokingly created a contract where his wife signed in agreement of 10 days of uninterrupted play, allowing requests "at my convenience." 

The husband also reminded his wife that everything in the game is fictional.

Grand Theft Auto VI has drawn scrutiny from regulators and commentators for its heightened mature content, which includes strong sexual themes, nudity, strip club missions and satirical references to an in-game adult subscription brand modeled after OnlyFans. 

Those elements are among the features most concerning to spouses, according to social posts.

Relationship coach, podcaster and author Matthew Hussey weighed in on how couples can avoid letting GTA VI negatively affect their relationships. The Los Angeles-based expert acknowledged that it’s a "real problem" if a video game results in a partner not having their needs met.

WHY COUPLES SHOULD FLIRT WITH EACH OTHER EVERY DAY — PLUS THE ‘RED FLAG’ TO AVOID

Hussey noted that there are worse habits people can have, like staying out late drinking every night, although gaming does have the potential to become addictive.

In most cases, a new, exciting game release is a special interest and a passion that should be supported by one's partner, according to the expert.

Hussey argued that gaming deserves the same respect from partners as any other hobby, such as practicing jiu-jitsu, playing golf or going to the movies, rather than being treated as something to shame.

"If we know GTA 6 is about to come out, and it's really important to them, and they've been looking forward to it, we should be the ones saying, 'How do we carve out more time for you this week to go and play? Because I know this is a big moment for you,'" he said.

THE MARRIAGE WARNING SIGN THAT MAY BE WORSE THAN FIGHTING — AND 4 WAYS TO TURN THINGS AROUND

While it's healthy to support a partner’s hobby, it shouldn't come at the expense of the relationship, Hussey noted.

"If you're suddenly at a point where you're like, 'I'm not getting my needs met, and I literally am coming second to this video game all the time,' then that's a real conversation [that needs to be had]," he said.

While sexually explicit gameplay can cause friction for some couples, Hussey called it "interesting," comparing it to reading popular, steamy "romantasy" novels.

"If my wife was reading a romance novel, and she was fantasizing things that she was reading in that book, I don't mind. It's a book, it's fantasy," he said. "I think the reverse argument might be made in some ways for GTA VI, where it's not living in the world of reality."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Hussey cautioned that interactions in a game should not become a "surrogate" for the real thing, pulling one partner away from a real-life relationship.

"[If] you're doing things for a character in a game, like you haven't texted your wife back, but you are worried about texting your character girlfriend back ... that's a different story, and I think that's a real problem."

The expert said he’s more worried about single people who don’t have a partner who can "call them out" if they’re spending too much time in a fictional reality.

"There's no one there to ring the alarm and say, 'You're on your 14th night in the house, and you haven't interacted with a real person or given yourself a real shot at finding love,'" he said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"I think video games are awesome. … We're just going to have to be really disciplined about asking ourselves, 'Am I still investing in real relationships or has this become a surrogate for them?'"

Bringing up unmet needs caused by excessive gaming can be difficult for couples. Hussey suggests starting not with criticism, but by showing you have your partner’s best interests at heart.

It's important to clarify that you aren't trying to take away a hobby they love, and instead are framing it around your own needs, he added.

"Somewhere in the process you're starting to feel overlooked, and there are things that are important to you that you don't feel like you're getting," he said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"If you show someone ... that you genuinely care about their happiness and them getting their needs met … they're not seeing someone who's at odds with them," he went on. 

"It's not an antagonistic conversation. It's someone looking at you as their teammate."

Framing the conversation this way encourages reciprocity, Hussey said, prompting a partner to think, "I better get my act together, because this isn't a given that I would have a partner who's this supportive of me."

item.description: Army cadets snuck in after 1:00 a.m. to change "Go Navy" to "Go Army" before Navy vs. Memphis, keeping the rivalry alive despite NIL and the transfer portal era.
item.content:encoded:
With all the talk of rivalries being a thing of the past, or at the very least devalued with the rise of NIL, the transfer portal, expansion of the College Football Playoff to 24 teams starting in the 2027 season and the elimination of conference championship games after this season, it's nice to see a prank between teams to add fuel to a rivalry fire.

THESE ONCE-ANNUAL COLLEGE RIVALRIES USED TO DEFINE COLLEGE FOOTBALL AND NEED TO MAKE A COMEBACK ASAP

Few rivalries in sports carry the history, tradition and patriotic significance of the Army vs. Navy football game, appropriately nicknamed "America's Game." Dating back to 1890, the annual showdown between the Army Black Knights and Navy Midshipmen is about far more than football. It's a celebration of military service, sacrifice, brotherhood and the young men who will one day defend our country. While the two academies are bitter rivals on the field, they're united in their commitment to serving the United States.

That respect as service members didn't stop a few Army cadets from pulling off the ultimate prank prior to the Navy vs. Memphis game on Saturday, though.

"Earlier this morning, a group of Army cadets pulled off the ultimate prank," ESPN2's sideline reporter Morgan Uber said on the broadcast. "This is a rivalry that goes on all year long. These cadets, in uniform, snuck in after 1:00 a.m. to change 'Go Navy' to 'Go Army' in the stands here."

item.title: Former press secretary Katie Zacharia criticizes GOP over midterm losses, says party isn’t ‘good at winning’
item.description: Katie Zacharia, who served just five days as White House press secretary, says Republicans are "terrible at the offense" after losing nine Senate seats.
item.content:encoded:
Former White House press secretary Katie Zacharia offered a blunt assessment of her party’s midterm collapse, saying Republicans lack the offensive instincts needed to win elections.

Speaking with The Free Press, Zacharia — who served as press secretary for just five days in October — weighed in on what she believes led to Democrats’ historic midterm sweep earlier this month.

"There’s nobody persuasive in the Democrats, but they’ve always banked on Trump Derangement Syndrome," Zacharia told the outlet.

VOTERS WANT TO 'MOVE ON' FROM THE PRESIDENT, FORMER TRUMP OFFICIAL CLAIMS AS REASON FOR GOP'S MIDTERM DEFEAT

She then took aim at her own party as she looked to cast blame for Republicans losing nine Senate seats and at least 50 seats in the House of Representatives to Democratic challengers.

"The Republicans are terrible at the offense," she added. "I mean, we can’t win. We’re not good at winning."

LEAVITT REVEALS WHAT REPUBLICANS MUST DO TO SURVIVE POLITICALLY AFTER TRUMP LEAVES WHITE HOUSE

However, Zacharia appeared to not harbor any ill-will toward her former boss, telling The Free Press that she does not intend to spill any secrets about the White House because "there’s nothing terrible to write."

"President Trump made me famous," Zacharia said, boasting about her relationship with Trump. "I can’t even keep up. I had to hire someone to go track all my opportunities."

WHITE HOUSE REPORTERS REACT TO KATIE ZACHARIA'S 'BRUTAL' EXIT AS TRUMP'S PRESS SECRETARY

Zacharia departed her position after Trump revealed to reporters that he told her, "You don't have to do this if you don't want to. I think you should reconsider."

She left the role after a rocky showing before the White House press corps and several controversies over her legal credentials after she took office.

LEAVITT OPENS UP ON HELPING TRUMP FIND NEW PRESS SECRETARY AFTER ZACHARIA DEBACLE: 'WAS NOT FOR HER'

Despite her short tenure in the White House, Zacharia reportedly remains in lockstep with Trump on certain topics — both social and political.

Earlier this month, the president sat down for an interview on CBS’s "60 Minutes," where correspondent Ross Douthat asked whether he would consider forgiving his political enemies if faced with the decision while standing at the gates of Heaven.

"I probably cannot do that, no, because I do hate some of my enemies and I always will," Trump replied.

Zacharia appeared to agree with the president on the topic of forgiveness, telling The Free Press that she has found it difficult to pray for her own enemies.

"I respect him for saying it," Zacharia said. "That’s how we all feel. I had friends telling me after everything that happened that I needed to be praying for my enemies, and I was like, ‘No, justice is the Lord’s, and sometimes you want to see retribution for those who have harmed you.’"

REPUBLICANS NEED HISTORY LESSON ABOUT THEIR PARTY IF THEY WANT TO MOVE ON FROM DEFEAT

She went on to say that she would not offer forgiveness to the alleged killer of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, adding, "Erika [Kirk] might be able to, but I can't."

Zacharia’s comments regarding religion and forgiveness sparked criticism from Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff, who told Fox News Digital that her stance is surprisingly in conflict with her Christian faith.

"What jumped out to me was how casually she agreed with Trump that you shouldn’t forgive or pray for your enemies," Shroff said. "Republicans talk constantly about Christian values, but apparently one of Christianity’s clearest teachings becomes negotiable when Trump has a grievance."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Shroff went on to point to Democratic Sen.-elect James Talarico’s use of religion in his successful campaign in Texas — a move that marked a significant shift surrounding the party’s appetite for religious candidates.

"We saw James Talarico succeed at pointing out a lot of those double standards when it comes to faith on the right," Shroff told Fox News Digital. "So it does seem that Republicans have ceded ground on the topic of faith with all of the Trump administration and MAGA hypocrisy around it."

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House and Zacharia for comment.

item.title: With each 3, Tennessee hoops sharp-shooter is helping wins pile up while making kids' wildest dreams come true
item.description: Tyler Lundblade's 3-pointers fuel Tennessee basketball and the Swishes for Wishes drive, with fans donating to Make-A-Wish East Tennessee each make.
item.content:encoded:
With 30 attempts from long range so far this season, Tyler Lundblade has already put up more 3-pointers than any other player on the Tennessee men’s basketball team.

Not that anyone wants him to stop.

Not only is 3-point shooting Lundblade’s thing — to the tune of more than 100 in each of the previous two seasons and a personal record of 9 in one game — made 3-pointers for Lundblade carry an even bigger meaning this season.

As OutKick turns to Knoxville for today’s college football Game of the Week between Tennessee and visiting LSU, there’s also big news happening on campus with Lundblade’s undefeated (5-0) and nationally-ranked Volunteers. And not just on the hardwood.

WILL TENNESSEE ZOOM PAST NO. 1 TEXAS? THESE VOLS COMPETING IN AUTO INNOVATION HAVE ALREADY HIT THE GAS

Lundblade has partnered with Make-A-Wish East Tennessee this season. And every time he makes a 3-pointer, fans who are taking part in this year’s "Swishes For Wishes" initiative will make a donation that is used to fund wishes for children in the area who are battling serious illnesses.

"My parents always preached to steward what we have and that’s a huge reason I play basketball," said Lundblade, who has connected on 8 shots from downtown so far this season. "I wanted to do something with this platform, with my 3-pointers, and it just gives me such a huge joy to give back."

While at Belmont over the previous two years, Lundblade, who transferred to Tennessee for his sixth year, set back-to-back school records for made 3-pointers. He first hit 104 3-pointers and then broke that record the very next season with 115 3-pointers. He would like to drain well over 100 3-pointers again this season.

Doing so well help kids like Axel. Lundblade recently met Axel, who was granted the wish of "the ultimate Tennessee football game-day experience." Except that game-day experience turned into a two-day dream in which Axel did all kinds of things on the Knoxville campus, including shooting baskets with Lundblade.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The two also opened gifts, took pictures and just hung out.

"It’s a blast to get to know (the kids)," said Lundblade, who has started four of five games and averages 23 minutes a game for the No. 14 Volunteers, who recently crushed No. 2 Michigan State. He’s averaging 8.2 points per game. "And to actually be a part of a wish being granted was awesome."

Make-A-Wish East Tennessee is a chapter of the national Make-A-Wish organization. It serves 36 counties in east Tennessee and last year granted 123 wishes, at an average of $10,000 per wish. Wishes have included trips to Disney World, Hawaii and France, shopping sprees, celebrity meet-ups and access to big entertainment and sporting events.

"The kids get really creative with their wishes and we do a lot of fun wishes," said Bridgitte Lucas, Development Manager for Make-A-Wish East Tennessee. "'Swishes for Wishes' has been such a fun campaign for basketball fans, donors, just the community to sort of rally around Tyler and have something really exciting to track when going to the games."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Lucas says Make-A-Wish East Tennessee is already looking into partnering with other teams on campus. "Homers for Hope" with the baseball team might roll out next.

For Lundblade, he’ll move on at the end of the season, but he seems committed to serving elsewhere. He’s grown up with that mentality and was looking for a way to be involved in a charitable initiative this season even before Make-A-Wish approached him.

"I tell people all the time, the greatest gift I’ve had in my life is two parents that love the Lord and serve him authentically," Lundblade said. "This game is a really easy way to share my faith and help others and I give a large credit to my parents because of the way they raised us and the example they set for us."

Next up for Lundblade and Tennessee is a tilt on Tuesday afternoon against Maryland at the Players Era 16 tournament in Las Vegas.
